walk/fwd: To backprop through a graph, first run it forward and keep every value. With x two, z three and c minus four: q is six, r is two, and f is four.
walk/seed: Then start at the output, where the gradient of f with respect to itself is one.
walk/sq: Walk back one node at a time. At each, multiply the gradient from above by the node's local slope. The square's slope is two r, which is four, so r gets one times four: four.
walk/add: The add passes that four, unchanged, to both q and c.
walk/mul: The multiply swaps: x gets z times four, twelve, and z gets x times four, eight.
walk/all: So the gradient is twelve for x, eight for z, and four for c. One backward walk gives every one of them.
twice/fork: Sometimes one value feeds two nodes. Here x goes into the multiply, and also straight into the add.
twice/paths: Walking back, x receives a gradient along each wire: one from the add, and from the multiply, z times one, which is two.
twice/sum: The two add up: x's total gradient is three. Nudge x, and f moves through both paths at once, so their effects add.
